newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Punjab state to go to polls on February 6.
newsitem.headline: India's Punjab state to go to polls on February 6.

text.p: The northern Indian state of Punjab, which witnessed a troubled decade of Sikh separatist violence in the 1980s, will hold state assembly elections on February 6, election officials said on Monday.
Election Commission spokesman Subas Pani told Reuters that elections to the state's 117 constituencies will begin formally with an official notification on January 13.
Punjab last held assembly elections amid tight security in 1992 after India contained prolonged separatist violence by Sikh religious extremists.
Pani said election officials would maintain security to ensure safe polling this year, but were not expected to face any major threat.
Parliamentary elections held in May were largely peaceful in the agriculturally rich state.
The separatist problem peaked in 1984, when Indian army troops entered the Golden Temple, Sikhism's holiest shrine, to flush out heavily-armed Sikh militants.

That incident provoked widespread anger among Sikhs. Four months later, the then Indian prime minister, Indira Gandhi, was shot dead by two of her own Sikh bodyguards upset by the army's entry into the holy shrine.

The United News of India said elections for three lower house (Lok Sabha) seats in the federal parliament from the northern states of Punjab and Uttar Pradesh and northwestern Rajasthan will be held simultaneously with the Punjab local poll.
